reason: I re-read ADR.md (249 lines), SAD.md and SRS.md from disk. The ADR matches the SAD on the stack (FastAPI, pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2.x, Alembic v1 to v3, asyncio.TaskGroup, create_subprocess_exec), the layering contract and the forbidden-sqlalchemy sources. All 11 ADRs have Status, Context, Decision, Rationale, Consequences and Alternatives Considered. The three earlier SAD caveats are handled: the AC-N6.2 wording conflict is carried as a Requires Verification open item in ADR-002. ADR-011 openly states that the brief's circuit breaker, atomic write and ThreadPoolExecutor are absent from the SAD, so it invents nothing. Only the template-format check was not compared against the template file itself.

gaps.message: ADR.md adds an 'Alternatives Considered' subsection that the template's Status/Context/Decision/Rationale/Consequences headings do not list. The review checklist requires documenting alternatives, so this is a harmless superset of the template.

The SPEC says 'repository 以外的任何層' may not import sqlalchemy, but the ADR-002 forbidden contract names only api, service, config and errors as sources. ADR-002 flags this as Requires Verification, and it still needs confirmation from the SPEC owner.
ADR-011 has status 'Proposed (Requires Verification)', which leaves one ADR not Accepted. This is acceptable because it records non-adoption, but it should be closed once the SPEC owner confirms.
